Nxeon (Hostinger-clone VPS/hosting platform, Next.js + Prisma + Proxmox, at /opt/nxeon) just bought its first non-OVH physical server: a Hetzner dedicated box in Falkenstein, Germany (auction server #3068915, i7-8700, 64GB RAM, includes one IPv4 178.63.94.114 + an IPv6 /64 subnet, unlimited traffic). The owner wants: (1) provider identifiers (OVH, Hetzner) and region identifiers on nodes, (2) region identifiers on IPs too, (3) this new node actually added/integrated into the fleet. Design a concrete implementation plan — this is Phase 4 quality, ready to execute, not a survey of options.

## Ground truth from a completed research pass (verified against the real code, trust this over re-deriving it)

**`Node` model** (`prisma/schema.prisma:1131-1157`) already supports multiple rows (doc comment: "additional nodes are onboarded via scripts/onboard-node.sh") but has NO provider or region field today — only `name` (unique label) and `pveNode` (Proxmox's own node name). Fields: `id, name, pveNode, apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, publicIp, bridge, subnetPrefix, ipStart, ipEnd, sshPortStart, sshPortEnd, natChain, storageNvme, storageHdd, capacityRamMB, isPrimary, enabled, status (NodeStatus: ONLINE|OFFLINE|MAINTENANCE), lastSeenAt, createdAt`, relation `servers Server[]`. Live DB: exactly ONE Node row today (`name="primary"`, `pveNode="ns5002569"`, `publicIp="51.79.162.96"`, `isPrimary=true`).

**`lib/proxmox.ts`** (921 lines) already has a real multi-node primitive: `export type NodeConn = { apiUrl: string; pveNode: string; tokenId: string; tokenSecret: string }` (shaped 1:1 to Node's own fields) and `pveFor(conn: NodeConn): PveClient` (line 87-117, comment: "Use in the worker for multi-node") which builds a fully independent client. BUT several standalone functions still hardcode the single env-derived singleton `pve`/`NODE` (from `PROXMOX_API_URL`/`PROXMOX_NODE`/`PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID`/`PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET` env vars) instead of taking a `PveClient`: `waitForTask` (119-132), `nextVmid` (263-266), `vmStatus` (476-478), `nodeStatus` (480-482), `listVms` (484-486), `nodeRrd` (497-499), `listSnapshots` (676-679), `listBackups` (681-684), `storageStatus` (919-921). Node-conn-aware siblings already exist in parallel for some of these (`vmRrd` at 491-495 takes an optional `conn?: PveClient`, `listBackupsOn` at 792-798, `archivedVmids` at 464-474, the `TaskClient`/`waitForTaskProgress` machinery at 138-261). THIS IS A REAL LATENT BUG that becomes an actual customer-facing correctness problem the moment a second node has real customers: e.g. `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` calls `vmStatus(server.vmid)` with no node argument, so a customer on the NEW Hetzner node would see the PRIMARY OVH node's stats for a same-numbered vmid (or an error/wrong-VM data) instead of their own server's real CPU/mem/uptime. Same bug independently affects `lib/discord-status-command.ts`'s `/status` slash command (built earlier this session), which also calls bare `vmStatus(s.vmid)`.

**Node selection / scheduling**: `lib/node-capacity.ts:340-361`, `scheduleNode(planRamMB)` — already multi-node-aware, bin-packs by free RAM % across `db.node.findMany({ where: { enabled: true, status: "ONLINE" } })`, no provider/region weighting today (not required to add any — RAM-only is fine to keep). Called from `lib/order.ts:666`, `lib/game-order.ts:348`, `lib/actions-nxcloud.ts:107`, `lib/custom-plan.ts:119`. `lib/order.ts:660-668` already lets a customer explicitly pick `intent.nodeId` from the deploy wizard, falling back to `scheduleNode` otherwise. `worker/index.ts:109-118`, `nodeFor(server)`, already resolves the correct per-server Proxmox client via `pveFor` at 11 call sites — the WORKER layer is already fully multi-node-correct; the gap is entirely in customer-facing dashboard reads and the Discord status command.

**Customer-facing multi-node UI ALREADY EXISTS and activates automatically**: `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:50,319,1063-1076` — `type NodeOpt = { id, name, publicIp }`, `const multiNode = nodes.length > 1`, a "Choose a location" step — sourced from `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:57`'s `db.node.findMany({ where: { enabled: true }, select: { id, name, publicIp } })`. Today it shows only `name`+`publicIp` per node (no region/provider, because neither field exists yet) — once a 2nd enabled Node row exists this step already turns on with zero other code changes, but should be extended to show the new region info once it exists so customers can actually tell nodes apart meaningfully (right now two nodes would look identical except for name/IP).

**IP pool — `DedicatedIp`** (`prisma/schema.prisma:1070-1086`): FLAT AND GLOBAL, hardcoded to exactly one OVH server via an ENV VAR, not a DB column: `lib/dedicated-ip.ts:41`, `const SERVER = process.env.OVH_SERVER_NAME ?? "ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net"`. Fields: `id, address (unique), ovhBlock, virtualMac?, status (FREE|ASSIGNED|PENDING|RELEASING), serverId? (unique FK to Server), server?, reverse?, purpose (CUSTOMER|INTERNAL), purposeLabel?, createdAt`. NO `nodeId`, no provider/region. Every OVH call in `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` (`syncDedicatedIpPool`, `findVirtualMacForIp`, `allocateDedicatedIp`, `releaseDedicatedIp`) hardcodes that same single `SERVER` constant. `ovhGateway()` (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts:73-77`) derives the failover gateway from a single `PUBLIC_IP` env var's `/24`'s `.254` — an OVH-specific failover-IP convention. Live DB: 9 rows total (1 FREE, 5 ASSIGNED customer, 3 ASSIGNED internal), all against the one OVH server. This has NO way today to have a second IP pool for a different physical server/provider — this is a real, required schema+code change, not optional.

**`lib/ovh.ts`** (92 lines): `ovhConfigured()`, `ovh(method, path, body)` (signed AK/AS/CK client), `ovhApi.{me,servers,server,ips,ipInfo,virtualMacs,createVirtualMac,setReverse}`. Direct importers: `app/admin/ips/page.tsx`, `worker/index.ts`, `scripts/set-mail-ptr.ts`, `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`. `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` itself is imported far more widely (~25 files) — every one of those transitively assumes an OVH-only pool.

**No existing Region/Provider convention anywhere** — grepped the whole schema for region/location/datacenter; only unrelated hits (`Visit.region`, `GeoCache.region` for marketing geo-analytics, `Business.region` for CRM leads). Nothing to collide with or reuse; this is a genuinely new concept for infra.

**Node has NO SSH fields** (confirmed by grep) — the platform talks to Proxmox hosts exclusively via the token-authenticated Proxmox API (`apiUrl`+`tokenId`+`tokenSecret`), never direct root SSH to the hypervisor host itself. (Contrast: `HostingNode`, a separate model for the shared-hosting box, DOES have SSH fields, because that product manages the box directly over SSH — not relevant here, this is a normal Proxmox compute node.) `scripts/onboard-node.sh` is the existing runbook for bringing up a new node — read it if present, it presumably already sets up Proxmox + the API token + firewall/NAT chain on a fresh host, and would need to be run (via SSH, one-time, to get the Node row's `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` in the first place) against the new Hetzner box. Its own header notes each node NATs its own private /24 behind its own public IP and VMs on different physical hosts CANNOT reach each other privately (no cross-host overlay exists) — worth a one-line callout in the plan as a known limitation, not something to build a fix for now.

## What to design

1. **Schema additions** (additive, safe to `db push` on staging then production): a `provider` concept on `Node` (OVH vs Hetzner — decide enum vs validated string, considering the codebase's own convention of enums for small STABLE sets like `NodeStatus`/`DedicatedIpStatus` vs plain strings for fast-growing sets like `StaffGrant.area`) and a `region` concept (datacenter code, e.g. "sgp"/"fsn1" — this will grow much faster than providers, so lean toward the plain-string convention, matching how the codebase already handles fast-changing categorical values elsewhere). Decide whether `DedicatedIp` should get its own denormalized region/provider fields, or a `nodeId` FK to `Node` and derive provider/region via the relation (avoids duplication/drift) — recommend the relational approach given the codebase's general FK-based conventions, but note the real tradeoff: existing 9 `DedicatedIp` rows need a backfill migration to the primary Node's id.

2. **`lib/hetzner.ts`** — a new Robot API client mirroring `lib/ovh.ts`'s exact shape (`hetznerConfigured()`, `hetzner(method, path, body)` using HTTP Basic Auth per Hetzner Robot API docs, `hetznerApi` wrappers for whatever this integration actually needs: listing/ordering additional IPs on the new server, server reset/rescue, reverse DNS). Keep it minimal — only what `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s generalized flow actually needs to call, don't build a kitchen-sink client.

3. **Generalizing `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`** away from its single hardcoded OVH `SERVER` constant into something that can serve a pool per node/provider — design the minimal correct change (e.g. a provider-dispatch inside `allocateDedicatedIp`/`releaseDedicatedIp`/`syncDedicatedIpPool` keyed off the IP's now-real `nodeId` → `node.provider`, OVH branch keeps the existing virtualMac dance unchanged, Hetzner branch is simpler per the plumbing this session already confirmed works differently — no virtual MAC needed, Hetzner routes additional IPs straight to the server's real MAC). Must not break any of the ~25 existing importers' current OVH-only behavior — this is an additive/branching change, not a rewrite.

4. **Fixing the real correctness bug**: the standalone `lib/proxmox.ts` functions that hardcode the primary-node singleton and are reachable for a customer on a DIFFERENT node — scope this precisely to the functions that are ACTUALLY reachable from customer-facing code for a non-primary-node server (start with `vmStatus`, since that's the one already confirmed reachable from both `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` and `lib/discord-status-command.ts`; check whether `listSnapshots`/`listBackups`/`nextVmid` are similarly reachable from customer/staff-facing code for a specific server, vs. only ever used in admin/fleet-wide contexts where the primary-node assumption might be intentional). Propose the exact fix shape: likely a `vmStatusFor(conn: PveClient, vmid)` sibling matching the existing `vmRrd`/`listBackupsOn` pattern, with call-site updates threading the server's actual node connection through (reusing `worker/index.ts`'s `nodeFor`-style resolution, or a shared equivalent for page/component contexts).

5. **Actually onboarding the physical node**: what real steps are needed (read `scripts/onboard-node.sh` if it exists to describe them precisely, don't invent) to go from "a fresh Hetzner box" to "a working `Node` row" — likely: run the onboarding script over SSH against the new box's IP (178.63.94.114) using its Hetzner root password, which installs Proxmox + creates the API token + sets up the NAT chain/bridge, then use the existing `lib/actions-nodes.ts`'s `addNode` (or the DB directly) to create the `Node` row with the new `provider`/`region` fields populated, then verify with the existing `testNode` action.

6. **Extending the deploy wizard's "Choose a location" step** to actually show provider/region now that the data exists (small, low-risk UI change to `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` and `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`'s node query).

Produce a phased, concrete plan (schema → hetzner client → dedicated-ip generalization → proxmox.ts correctness fix → node onboarding runbook → UI) with exact file paths, reusing every existing function/pattern named above rather than inventing new ones. Flag any place you're genuinely uncertain and would want to ask the owner a clarifying question rather than guessing (e.g. the region-code naming convention, whether to fix ALL of the hardcoded proxmox.ts functions now or just the customer-visible ones, whether the Hetzner IPv6 /64 subnet needs any special handling vs the IPv4).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
# =============================================================================
# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
# current state before changing anything.
#
# What it does:
#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
#      needs (documented pveum commands)
#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
#
# SAFETY:
#   - Never flushes the firewall. It only APPENDS its own MASQUERADE/FORWARD
#     rules and only if an identical rule is not already present.
#   - Never touches running VMs. Template builds skip any VMID that exists.
#   - Never destroys storage. `pvesm add` is skipped when the storage id exists.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CROSS-HOST NETWORKING — IMPORTANT LIMITATION (read before deploying node #2)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each node NATs its OWN private /24 (10.20.N.0/24) behind its OWN public IP.
# This makes each node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation and
# SSH DNAT — but it does NOT give VMs on different physical hosts a shared LAN.
#
#   * A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the
#     private network. They are separate NAT islands.
#   * The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the
#     DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on.
#
# If you need private east-west connectivity between VMs on different nodes you
# must lay an overlay/VPN over the public IPs — e.g. WireGuard mesh or a VXLAN
# fabric (Proxmox SDN "VXLAN zone") — and route the /24s across it. That is out
# of scope for this script; it is a deliberate, documented follow-up. For the
# common case (independent single-node VPS customers) per-node NAT islands are
# exactly what you want.
#
# Assumption: node #2 is a SEPARATE physical box with its own public IP, NOT a
# second NIC on the same L2 as node #1. If two nodes truly share L2 you would
# instead give them the SAME bridge/subnet and split the IP range — but this
# script assumes the separate-host model above.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ---------- Parameters (flags override env) ----------------------------------
NODE_NUM="${NODE_NUM:-2}"           # ordinal; drives subnet + nat chain defaults
SUBNET_OCTET=""                     # third octet of 10.20.X.0/24 (default: NODE_NUM-1)
PUBLIC_IP="${PUBLIC_IP:-}"          # this host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if empty)
BRIDGE=""                           # vmbrX (default: vmbr1)
NVME_STORAGE="${NVME_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
HDD_STORAGE="${HDD_STORAGE:-vmdata-hdd}"
NVME_ZPOOL="${NVME_ZPOOL:-}"        # existing ZFS pool for NVMe storage (optional)
HDD_DIR="${HDD_DIR:-/tank/backup}"  # dir-backed HDD storage path
SNIPPETS_STORAGE="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE:-$HDD_STORAGE}"
TOKEN_USER="${TOKEN_USER:-nxeon@pve}"
TOKEN_NAME="${TOKEN_NAME:-platform}"
TOKEN_ROLE="${TOKEN_ROLE:-NxeonProvision}"
BUILD_TEMPLATES="${BUILD_TEMPLATES:-0}"   # 1 = build 9000-9004 here; 0 = document copying
SSH_PORT_START="${SSH_PORT_START:-20000}"
SSH_PORT_END="${SSH_PORT_END:-29999}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [flags]
  --node-num N          Node ordinal (default 2). Sets defaults for subnet + nat chain.
  --subnet-octet N      Third octet of the /24 (default: node-num - 1, e.g. node 2 -> 1 -> 10.20.1.0/24).
  --public-ip IP        This host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if omitted).
  --bridge vmbrX        NAT bridge name (default vmbr1).
  --nvme-storage NAME   NVMe storage id (default vmdata).
  --hdd-storage NAME    HDD storage id (default vmdata-hdd).
  --nvme-zpool POOL     Existing ZFS pool to back the NVMe storage (zfspool). Optional.
  --hdd-dir PATH        Directory for the HDD (dir) storage (default /tank/backup).
  --build-templates     Build cloud-init templates 9000-9004 on this host.
  -h, --help            Show this help.

Environment variables mirror the flags (NODE_NUM, PUBLIC_IP, BRIDGE, ...).
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --node-num) NODE_NUM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --subnet-octet) SUBNET_OCTET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --public-ip) PUBLIC_IP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bridge) BRIDGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-storage) NVME_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-storage) HDD_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-zpool) NVME_ZPOOL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-dir) HDD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --build-templates) BUILD_TEMPLATES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown flag: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# ---------- Derived values ---------------------------------------------------
[[ -z "$SUBNET_OCTET" ]] && SUBNET_OCTET="$((NODE_NUM - 1))"
[[ -z "$BRIDGE" ]] && BRIDGE="vmbr1"
SUBNET_PREFIX="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}."
SUBNET_CIDR="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.0/24"
GATEWAY_IP="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.1"
if [[ "$NODE_NUM" -le 1 ]]; then
  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD"
else
  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD_N${NODE_NUM}"
fi
PVE_NODE="$(hostname)"
[[ -z "$PUBLIC_IP" ]] && PUBLIC_IP="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"

log()  { echo -e "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
ok()   { echo -e "  \033[32m✓\033[0m $*"; }
warn() { echo -e "  \033[33m!\033[0m $*"; }

require_root() { [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "Run as root on the Proxmox host." >&2; exit 1; }; }
require_cmd()  { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing required command: $1" >&2; exit 1; }; }

require_root
require_cmd pvesm
require_cmd pveum
require_cmd iptables

log "Onboarding node #${NODE_NUM} — ${PVE_NODE} (${PUBLIC_IP})"
log "  subnet ${SUBNET_CIDR} via ${BRIDGE} (gw ${GATEWAY_IP}), NAT chain ${NAT_CHAIN}"

# =============================================================================
# 1 + 2. NAT bridge + ip_forward + MASQUERADE
# =============================================================================
log "[1/7] NAT bridge ${BRIDGE} (${GATEWAY_IP}/24)"
if ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "bridge ${BRIDGE} already exists — leaving it as-is"
else
  # Append an isolated (no physical port) NAT bridge to /etc/network/interfaces.
  # We do NOT reload all interfaces (that could disrupt the host); we bring up
  # just this bridge with ifup.
  if ! grep -qE "^\s*auto\s+${BRIDGE}\b" /etc/network/interfaces 2>/dev/null; then
    cat >>/etc/network/interfaces <<EOF

# --- Nxeon node #${NODE_NUM} NAT bridge (added by onboard-node.sh) ---
auto ${BRIDGE}
iface ${BRIDGE} inet static
        address ${GATEWAY_IP}/24
        bridge-ports none

onboard-hosting-node.sh
onboard-node.sh
---
384 scripts/onboard-node.sh

I explored the actual code at `/opt/nxeon` (not `/opt/nxeon/app` — that path doesn't exist; the real app root is `/opt/nxeon`) and confirmed every claim in the ground-truth brief against the live files, plus found several things the brief didn't call out that materially change scope/sequencing. Findings and the concrete plan follow.

## Things I confirmed that change the plan

1. **Schema is managed by `prisma db push`, with a hard standing rule against any agent running it.** `/opt/nxeon/prisma/manual-migrations/2026-08-29-domain-order-intent.sql` is a precedent: the schema change goes into `prisma/schema.prisma`, and a **hand-reviewable SQL file** matching Prisma's own DDL conventions goes into `prisma/manual-migrations/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.sql` with a comment saying it is NOT APPLIED and must be run by a human (`npx prisma db push` from a machine with `DATABASE_URL` set, or by hand). Whoever executes this plan must follow that exact pattern for the `Node.provider`/`Node.region`/`DedicatedIp.nodeId` additions — not run `db push` themselves.

2. **The dedicated-IP-generalization work is not actually load-bearing for getting the Hetzner box live.** The auction listing includes exactly one IPv4 (178.63.94.114) and one routed /64 — no spare "additional/failover" IPv4s to pool. `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s whole pool exists to hand out *extra* IPs beyond a node's own `publicIp`; a first Hetzner node with only its one IP can serve ordinary (NAT-based) VPS/game orders today with **zero** changes to `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` or a new `lib/hetzner.ts`. I've kept that work in the plan (the owner explicitly asked for provider-aware IP handling), but sequenced it as Phase 4b, after the node is already taking traffic, and flagged it as a question below.

3. **The "fix the proxmox.ts singleton bug" scope is bigger than just `vmStatus`, but the fix pattern already exists in the codebase in three places** — I found the exact shape to copy, not invent:
   - `app/api/metrics/route.ts` (already correct): looks up `server.node`, builds `pveFor(...)`, passes the conn into `vmRrd(vmid, timeframe, conn)`.
   - `lib/actions-backups-admin.ts`'s `requestRestore` (already correct): `if (server.node) { const client = pveFor(...); owned = await listBackupsOn(client, server.vmid) } else { owned = await listBackups(server.vmid) }` — with the comment "read from the server's own node (vmids can collide across nodes...)".
   - `lib/actions.ts`'s admin reconcile action (already correct): resolves `pveFor(node)` and calls `client.vmStatus(...)`.

   Every other per-server call site that still uses the bare singleton needs the identical treatment. Grepping all real call sites of `vmStatus(`, `listSnapshots(`, `listBackups(`, `nextVmid(`, `nodeStatus(`, `listVms(`, `nodeRrd(`, `storageStatus(` gives the complete, precise list:

   **Genuinely broken (per-server, reachable for a server that could be on any node) — must fix:**
   - `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:207-209` — `vmStatus(server.vmid)`, `listSnapshots(server.vmid)`, `listBackups(server.vmid)`. Its `db.server.findUnique` **already includes `node: true`** (line 124), so this is a pure call-site fix, no query change needed.
   - `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx:44` — `vmStatus(server.vmid)`. Its query does **not** currently include `node`; needs `node: true` added to the `include`.
   - `lib/discord-status-command.ts:62` — `vmStatus(s.vmid)`. Its `db.server.findMany` uses a `select` (not `include`), needs `node: { select: { apiUrl, pveNode, tokenId, tokenSecret } }` added.
